title: Preoperative mechanical prophylaxis in elderly patients with hip fracture
author: Nam JH
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.jfscjne

steps.title: Administer Preoperative Mechanical Thromboprophylaxis
steps.instruction: Apply mechanical thromboprophylaxis from the time of admission until surgery using an Intermittent Pneumatic Compression Device (IPCD) and Graduated Compression Stockings (GCS) simultaneously.

substeps.instruction: Apply IPCD (Kendall Express 9525 SCD: Covidien, Dublin, Ireland) garments to the calf and thigh of both legs.
Configure the IPCD pump to inflate and deflate every 35 to 45 seconds based on the patient's venous refilling time.
Set inflated pressures to 45 mmHg at the ankle, 40 mmHg in the calf, and 30 mmHg in the thigh.

steps.title: Administer Postoperative Chemical Prophylaxis
steps.instruction: Provide combined chemical prophylaxis for 10 to 14 days following the index surgery.

substeps.instruction: Commence subcutaneous administration of once-daily 40 mg enoxaparin 24 hours after the index surgery.
Continue medication for a total duration of 10 to 14 days.

steps.title: Administer Postoperative Mechanical Prophylaxis
steps.instruction: Continue mechanical thromboprophylaxis using IPCD and GCS simultaneously until discharge (approximately 2 weeks).

substeps.instruction: Maintain IPCD application to the calf and thigh of both legs.

steps.title: Implement Postoperative Rehabilitation
steps.instruction: Perform rehabilitation focused on early mobilization.

substeps.instruction: Initiate tolerable weight-bearing standing and ambulation using a walker two to three days after surgery.

steps.title: Monitor and Manage VTE
steps.instruction: Monitor for signs or symptoms of thromboembolic events within one month after the index surgery.

substeps.instruction: Perform 3-D CT angiography if VTE is clinically suspected.
Confirm DVT diagnosis via cardiovascular specialist and radiologist.
Confirm PE diagnosis via pulmonary specialist and radiologist.
Administer warfarin or rivaroxaban to all patients with confirmed VTE.
